description: Off-screen missions for a 13-15 year old. Not games: a thirteen year old spots a made-up task in a second and stops taking it seriously. Every mission here is real work with an effect other people can see — because what they are after at this age is to be useful, not to be busy. And the time floor is higher than for the 7-9 band because the same leverage factor is computed against a three-minute card.

missions.instruction_ar: Pick something you're good at — a game, a skill, a subject — and teach it to someone younger at home or in the family. Fifteen minutes, and you're the one explaining.
Not a sandwich — a meal. Pick it, make it, and serve it. And if it comes out wrong, the mistake is part of having made it yourself.
Not a text — a call. Your grandfather, your aunt, or whoever you haven't spoken to in a long time. Ask them about something that happened back when they were your age.
Something at home that's broken or won't work. Open it up, look for the fault, and give it a try. And if you can't figure it out, write down what the attempt taught you.

missions.title_ar: Walk for Half an Hour Without Your Phone
missions.instruction_ar: Leave your phone at home and walk. And when you get back, tell someone one thing you noticed that you wouldn't have noticed if you'd had it with you.
A neighbor, a classmate, or someone at home. Something that takes real effort, and without saying you're doing it for a mission.

missions.title_ar: Write Out Your Side of Something You Disagree With Your Parents About
missions.instruction_ar: Something you believe you're right about. Put it on half a page: your view, your argument, and the part where you might be wrong. Then sit down and read it with them.

missions.title_ar: Track Your Money for a Week
missions.instruction_ar: Write down every cent that comes in and goes out for a week. And at the end of the seventh day, look at the page and name one thing that surprised you.

missions.title_ar: Pray Fajr on Time for 3 Days
missions.instruction_ar: Three days in a row. And if you miss a day, you start again from the first — not as a punishment, but so that the three connect.

missions.title_ar: Clear Your Room of What You Don't Use
missions.instruction_ar: Look for things you haven't used in a year, and pick out what someone else could use. And deliver them yourself.

missions.title_ar: Read a Chapter and Tell It
missions.instruction_ar: One chapter of a book — paper, not a screen. Then tell it to someone at home in three minutes. And whatever you can't tell, you don't know.
Someone you were genuinely in the wrong with, even if it was a long time ago. Face to face or on a call — not by text.
